## Purpose {.unnumbered .unlisted}

\begin{marginfigure}
\mlagentstack{0}{0}{0}{0}{0}{100}
\end{marginfigure}

_What does a foundation-model invocation compute, and what contract does the rest of the computer need to use its output?_

An agentic system repeatedly invokes a foundation model to determine what to do next, but engineering reliability around these models requires treating the neural network as a physical hardware component: an unprivileged stochastic processor core. Conditioned on an array of discrete integer tokens staged in accelerator High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM), the core evaluates dense tensor contractions to propose candidate continuations under zero ambient authority—possessing no capability to read clocks, mutate files, open sockets, or verify truth. Translating this compute into an operational system exposes hard physical bottlenecks: Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) creates a severe structural impedance mismatch with programming language ASTs, while serial autoregressive generation collapses arithmetic intensity to memory-bandwidth-bound GEMV at single-agent batch sizes ($B=1$), forcing the entire parameter weight tensor across the memory bus for every token generated. Because statistical sequence likelihood decouples from operational correctness and stochastic models cannot verify their own invariants ($P < 1.0$), the host agent runtime must enclose the core within an asynchronous streaming ABI, protect against oracle poisoning via out-of-band evaluation, and enforce invariant closure through external deterministic verification. This chapter follows a single invocation from host-side token staging through parallel prefill and serialized decode to a caller-visible status envelope, establishing the processor boundary that necessitates deliberate inference-time compute in Chapter 3.

\newpage

::: {.callout-learning-objectives}

- Contrast the inverted execution model of the Stochastic Computer (Host OS in Ring 0 as sovereign master; neural core as unprivileged, stochastic Byzantine coprocessor under Zero Ambient Authority) with classical CPUs.
- Analyze Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) as host-side data marshaling at the PCIe DMA boundary, explaining the AST impedance mismatch and the JSON escaping penalty.
- Trace the autoregressive execution loop as stateful activation accumulation, explaining why next-token generation forms an irreducibly serial causal dependency chain at single-agent batch size ($B=1$).
- Decouple statistical sequence likelihood and text fluency from operational truth, specifying the external verification perimeter, differential baseline pre-flight testing, and out-of-band evaluation.
- Specify an asynchronous streaming invocation contract with explicit token/deadline limits, early cancellation semantics, and a normalized four-outcome status envelope.
- Explain grammar-constrained decoding via precompiled compressed bitmask tensors (XGrammar) and jump-forward decoding at the execution surface, distinguishing syntactic validity from semantic safety.
- Diagnose physical hardware bottlenecks: compute-bound GEMM prefill with $O(M^2)$ attention compute vs. memory-bandwidth-bound GEMV decode, the memory shuttle problem, NVLink all-reduce synchronization, and CUDA Graph launch amortization.
- Evaluate the twin pillars of agent latency: how prefix caching inverts Amdahl's Law to make speculative decoding mandatory, and how chunked prefill mitigates prefill-decode interference in continuous batching.
- Evaluate invocation interface designs (Native Tool Calling, Search/Replace block diffs, and interactive Bash REPLs) by downstream verified task success under equal resource budgets.

:::
